description: Reusable .NET 10 package that wraps ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie and JWT auth, Google OAuth, a pluggable e-mail provider, a multi-tenant model with dynamic RBAC (roles + module permissions), and secure defaults — wired up with a single AddMyIdentity call. JWT and Google OAuth secrets are supplied by the consumer (never shipped in the package).
releaseNotes: v4.0.0-alpha.21: an absent route scope becomes a configurable choice, the package ships its first Razor component, and a role's permission matrix can be written one module at a time -- read UPGRADE.md section 34. BREAKING (PERM-7): IMyIdentityPermissionAdminService gains UpsertRolePermissionAsync(roleId, moduleCode, permission, ct), returning the persisted MyIdentityRolePermission, and RemoveRolePermissionAsync(roleId, moduleCode, ct), returning bool. BREAKING only for hand-rolled implementers of that interface -- including a decorator that wraps it, and a hand-written test double -- who must add both methods; a consumer that only CALLS the interface, or that subclasses the shipped MyIdentityPermissionAdminService<TUser,TTenant,TContext>, is unaffected. Find yours with grep -rn "IMyIdentityPermissionAdminService" --include=*.cs --include=*.razor . run across the WHOLE solution, test projects included, and keep the hits that only call it. Until now the only supported way to persist a matrix edit was SaveRolePermissionsAsync, a replace of the role's ENTIRE matrix, so two admins editing DIFFERENT modules of the same role clobbered each other; they no longer do. Two admins on the SAME module remain last-writer-wins, which is typed conflict detection and is deliberately not solved here. UpsertRolePermissionAsync THROWS ArgumentException on MyIdentityPermission.None: as the argument of a single-module write it is ambiguous between removing the row and granting nothing, and those two are indistinguishable to the decision point -- call RemoveRolePermissionAsync to remove, or pass the permission the role should actually hold. SaveRolePermissionsAsync is UNCHANGED and still reads None as absence, deliberately: a whole-matrix replace describes a complete final state, where "absent" already means something, while a single-cell write says nothing about the rest of the matrix and the caller CHOSE to write None over one module. RemoveRolePermissionAsync invokes OnBeforePermissionsRemovedAsync -- which until now fired only from the whole-matrix path, so a consumer vetoing one removal had to rewrite the matrix to be asked -- and returns false rather than throwing when the row is already gone, including when a concurrent removal won the race; an unknown module code still throws. UpsertRolePermissionAsync instead RETRIES the whole read-modify-write on a DbUpdateException from the unique-index insert race, bounded by the same attempt budget SaveRolePermissionsAsync already uses, because the loser of an insert race still holds a value that must land. Both methods match and persist the CANONICAL module spelling, with the comparison performed by the database's collation inside the Where. A narrowing upsert does NOT invoke the removal hook: it removes bits, not a module. Added (AUTH-2): MyIdentityScopelessRouteBehavior { TenantWideOnly = 0, AnyScope = 1 } in MyIdentity.Authorization, exposed as MyIdentityPermissionOptions.ScopelessRouteBehavior. It governs ONE case -- what [MyIdentityRequirePermission] asks when no route value resolves a sub-scope -- and is not consulted at all when the route does carry one. The default is TenantWideOnly, identical to every previous release, so a consumer who sets nothing sees no behavioural change. AnyScope routes the check to HasPermissionInAnyContextAsync so a caller holding the permission in any single scope is admitted, which is the answer an application whose scope comes from a persistent UI selector rather than from the route actually needs. It is ADMISSION, NOT FILTERING: such a caller passes the screen gate and your data layer is the only thing narrowing rows from there. It is application-wide, governing every scopeless gate at once, with NO per-endpoint override. Added (AUTH-3): MyIdentityAuthorizeView in MyIdentity.Components, this package's first .razor file -- the same permission gate around a fragment -- with parameters ModuleCode, PermissionRequired, ScopeId (int?), ChildContent and NotAuthorized; consumers need @using MyIdentity.Components. It exists because <AuthorizeView Policy="..."> structurally cannot express the check: a policy name is composed at COMPILE time and a sub-scope is a RUNTIME value that changes per grid row. An omitted ScopeId is resolved by the AUTH-2 knob above, which is why the two ship together -- the page gate and the fragment gate can no longer disagree about an absent scope. It throws ArgumentException when PermissionRequired is MyIdentityPermission.None, making it the FOURTH gate to refuse None after the three AUTH-1 added in alpha.20, and the only one that throws during an END USER'S RENDER rather than at dev or startup time -- on Blazor Server that tears down the circuit for the whole page, so do not data-bind PermissionRequired to anything that can compute None. With FineGrainedPermissions:Enabled=false the component degrades to admins-only, exactly as the attribute does, because it consults the same IMyIdentityPermissionService. MyIdentity.csproj now emits InternalsVisibleTo("MyIdentity.Tests"), which grants nothing to any other assembly and changes nothing for consumers. API may still change before stable.
